registers.name: CTRL
registers.description: Control register. Host programs launch policy and safe-clear behavior. Writes are accepted only when the controller is not busy, except clear_fault semantics which are handled by the dedicated pulse register behavior in hardware.

fields.name: CFG_VALID
fields.description: Configuration-valid indicator. Software may use this as a compact software-managed validity bit for the programmed CSR set.

fields.name: AUTO_CLEAR_FAULT
fields.description: Optional host policy bit indicating that software intends to request a clear-fault action when safe. Actual sticky-fault clearing remains controlled by the hardware clear_fault path.

fields.name: RESERVED
fields.description: Reserved.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.description: Controller busy.

fields.name: DONE
fields.description: Operation completed.

fields.name: FAULT
fields.description: Sticky fault indicator.

fields.name: TIMEOUT
fields.description: Timeout fault sticky bit.

fields.name: STALE
fields.description: Stale-command fault sticky bit.

fields.name: CLAMPED
fields.description: Clamp indicator.

fields.name: FALLBACK_ACTIVE
fields.description: Safe fallback state active.

fields.name: TRANSPORT_ERROR
fields.description: Transport protocol error sticky bit.

registers.name: STATUS2
registers.description: Additional status bit for response validity.

fields.name: RESPONSE_VALID
fields.description: A bounded response has been accepted and parsed as command-relevant.

fields.name: RESERVED
fields.description: Reserved.

registers.name: LAUNCH
registers.description: Launch pulse register. Writing a 1 to bit 0 generates a one-cycle launch event when the controller is not busy and the launch is qualified.

fields.name: LAUNCH_PULSE
fields.description: Write-1 pulse to request a new model transaction.

fields.name: RESERVED

registers.name: CLEAR_FAULT
registers.description: Clear-fault pulse register. Writing a 1 to bit 0 requests sticky-fault clearing under the hardware safety policy.

fields.name: CLEAR_FAULT_PULSE
fields.description: Write-1 pulse to request sticky fault clearing when safe.

fields.name: RESERVED
fields.description: Reserved.

fields.description: Low byte of the compact response summary.

fields.name: RESPONSE_SUMMARY[15:8]
fields.description: Byte 1 of the compact response summary.

fields.name: RESPONSE_SUMMARY[23:16]
fields.description: Byte 2 of the compact response summary.

fields.name: RESPONSE_SUMMARY[31:24]

fields.name: RESPONSE_SUMMARY[39:32]
fields.description: Byte 4 of the compact response summary.

fields.name: RESPONSE_SUMMARY[47:40]
fields.description: Byte 5 of the compact response summary.

fields.name: RESPONSE_SUMMARY[55:48]
fields.description: Byte 6 of the compact response summary.

fields.name: RESPONSE_SUMMARY[63:56]

sources.name: FAULT
sources.description: Sticky fault indication suitable for optional software interrupt generation if system integration maps it.

sources.name: DONE
sources.description: Completion indication suitable for optional software interrupt generation if system integration maps it.

init_sequence: Hold reset_n low, then deassert reset_n.
Program SEQ_ID, TIMEOUT, FRESHNESS, VELOCITY, GEOMETRY_BASE, GEOMETRY_LENGTH, GEOMETRY_FORMAT, ACT_MIN, ACT_MAX, SLEW, CHECKPOINT, and FLAGS through the byte-wide CSR window.
Read STATUS and STATUS2 to confirm BUSY=0, FAULT=0, and RESPONSE_VALID=0.
Write CTRL.CFG_VALID=1 after configuration is complete.
If needed, request CLEAR_FAULT by writing 1 to CLEAR_FAULT, but only when software has determined the controller is safe to clear.
polling_sequence: Write LAUNCH=1 to start a transaction once configuration is valid.
Read STATUS, STATUS2, and RESP_SUMMARY[63:0] after completion.
If FAULT or TIMEOUT or STALE or TRANSPORT_ERROR is set, treat the output as invalid and rely on fallback behavior.
irq_sequence: If interrupts are enabled by the system integrator, map FAULT to a fault interrupt source and DONE to a completion interrupt source.
On fault interrupt, read STATUS and clear the fault only through the dedicated CLEAR_FAULT path when the system is safe.
On completion interrupt, read RESP_SUMMARY and the status bits before consuming cmd_value/cmd_rate outputs.

consistency_notes: All assumptions remain compatible with DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.
The register map is byte-wide and fits the preferred custom CSR window behavior described by the specification.
No additional hierarchy, ports, or external protocol assumptions are introduced.
Wide values are split across byte registers to match the 8-bit software-visible data path.
The map exposes only compact control, status, and summary fields and does not surface bulk geometry, flow fields, tensors, or per-point data.
